wage.note: Johansen trace and max-eigenvalue statistics (unrestricted constant, 4 lags in differences, data de-seasonalised by quarterly dummies first; 5% critical values from statsmodels, which assume no exogenous variables). The first eigenvector is normalised on the first variable.

imposed.source: BJN2003 Table 1 Panel 4 (0.09 (0.02) on u; coefficient on z = 1 imposed); BN2008 eq 50; NAM2026 eq 3.33: 0.12 on LFS unemployment (manufacturing)

unrestricted_eqcm.note: Wage equation with the levels (w − p − z)_{t−4} and u_{t−4} entered separately; γ_u = −(coefficient on u)/(coefficient on w − p − z).

price.note: Johansen trace and max-eigenvalue statistics (unrestricted constant, 4 lags in differences, data de-seasonalised by quarterly dummies first; 5% critical values from statsmodels, which assume no exogenous variables). The first eigenvector is normalised on the first variable.

unrestricted_eqcm.note: Price equation with p_{t−1}, (w + τ1 − z)_{t−1} and pi_{t−1} entered separately; the implied long-run weights are the ratios to the coefficient on p_{t−1}.

output.note: Output equation with y_{t−1}, g_{t−1}, rex_{t−1}, (RS − π)_{t−1} entered separately (plus the 2020Q2 dummy); implied long-run coefficients are ratios to the coefficient on y_{t−1}.

fx.note: BN2008 eq 36 finds −0.042 (t −3.5) on 1994Q2–2007Q2; NAM2026 Table 5.44 has no level term. The simulation uses the equation without the level term unless the 'PPP anchor' switch is on.

means.note: Sample means of the long-run components (lagged as they enter), so that moving γ_u, ϕ or the output long-run coefficients on the page keeps the equation's mean fit (the constant is re-centred as re-estimation of the constant alone would do).

construction_notes.pf: Foreign producer prices pf: euro-area domestic-output PPI (Eurostat, from 2000Q1) extended backwards with the German PPI's growth rates (1976Q1–1999Q4).
construction_notes.pstar: Foreign consumer prices p*: euro-area HICP (ECB, from 1996Q1) extended backwards with the German CPI's growth rates (OECD).
construction_notes.pen: Energy prices pe: composite of CPI 04.5 electricity, gas and other fuels (share 0.63) and 07.2.2 fuels and lubricants (0.37), StatBank 14700 from 2000Q3; before that its growth is backed out of ln(CPI) − ln(CPI excl. energy) with an estimated energy share of 0.072 (regression 2000Q4–latest, correlation with the actual series 0.97).
construction_notes.t1: Payroll-tax wedge τ1 = ln(1 + wage costs/wages − 1) from SSB's seasonally adjusted 09175 series (the unadjusted ratio has a ±2 pp seasonal that would otherwise enter the price EqCM).
construction_notes.t3: Indirect-tax term τ3 = ln(CPI) − ln(CPI-AT), available from 2003Q1; set to 0 before (a constant shift only).
construction_notes.tgt: Inflation target π̄: 2.5 to 2017Q4 (also used for 1996–2001Q1, before inflation targeting, where only the constant absorbs it), 2.0 from 2018Q1.
construction_notes.gap: Output gap: Hodrick–Prescott (λ = 1600) cycle of log mainland GDP, unadjusted, over the whole 1978Q1–latest sample (BJN App. B); end-point sensitivity applies.
construction_notes.u_seam: Registered unemployment: SSB/NAV unadjusted to 2014Q4, Norges Bank's seasonally adjusted history from 2015Q1; the unemployment equation therefore uses seasonal dummies only up to 2014Q4 (s1p–s3p).

estimator_note: Every equation is estimated by OLS. The published versions use FIML for the wage–price block (BJN2003, ABE2005, BN2008); here no contemporaneous endogenous regressor remains in the wage equation (Δ₄p enters lagged) and the price equation conditions on Δpi_t and Δpe_t, so OLS is consistent if the import-price and CPI disturbances are uncorrelated — see the residual correlation matrix. NAM2026 also estimates its equations one by one (§5.1).
